description: Scan manifests under `test/`, `tests/` and `__tests__/`: config:recommended ignores them via :ignoreModulesAndTests, but test harnesses in this org carry real dependencies, and a manifest Renovate never extracts can never receive a security PR.

Keep Renovate's default prCreation (immediate). CI in these repositories runs on pull requests, not on renovate/* branch pushes, so a branch has no status checks until its PR exists: not-pending or status-success would wait for checks that never start, and routine PRs would never open.

Renovate merges automerge PRs itself (platformAutomerge false) instead of arming GitHub's native auto-merge when it opens the PR. Native auto-merge waits only for the checks a branch rule marks as required. Renovate's own merge waits until nothing has failed, every check run it can see has finished as success, skipped or neutral, and every commit status other than its own passing renovate/* ones is success. Its own failed statuses (for example a lock file that failed to update) count as red, and a PR whose only statuses are its own passing ones stays pending. Checks and statuses from review bots count too, so this does not prove that CI ran: a repository that relies on automerge should require at least one CI status check. Do not set internalChecksAsSuccess: with it, a PR whose only status is the passing release-age check reads as green before CI has started.

packageRules.description: First-party cachekit-io packages propagate as fast as possible. They MUST have their own groupName: otherwise group:allNonMajor folds them into renovate/all-minor-patch, and that group follows the global (daily) schedule, silently overriding the at-any-time setting below (a grouped dep cannot keep its own schedule). With a dedicated group + no release-age quarantine (minimumReleaseAge defends against third-party supply-chain attacks, pointless for what we publish) + no schedule gate, an internal release (e.g. a cachekit-core patch) opens a dependent PR on the next hourly Renovate run. update-lockfile keeps the existing ^range and just bumps Cargo.lock. Major-version manual review still applies.

Lock file maintenance has no release timestamp, which Renovate reads as not yet aged; timestamp-optional stops its release-age status from staying pending forever. It never automerges. Like vulnerability PRs, it is exempt from the concurrent branch/PR caps, since it is how lockfile-only transitive alerts get fixed. Keep minimumReleaseAge set rather than null: npm refreshes derive their --before cutoff from it.
prBodyNotes: ⚠️ Renovate cannot check release age for lock file maintenance. npm refreshes get a best-effort `--before` from `minimumReleaseAge`, dropped if an artifact notice says it could not be applied; pnpm and yarn refreshes get only the repository's own package-manager setting (pnpm 11 defaults to one day). Review newly resolved versions before merging.

packageRules.description: No lock file maintenance for cargo or uv: their refreshes run with no release-age cutoff at all, and uv can build sdists while it resolves.
Auto-merge minor/patch dev dependencies after CI (age-gated by global minimumReleaseAge)
GitHub Actions: grouped manual review (CI infra blast radius)
wrangler never automerges, whatever its dependency type: it is the deploy tool, so every update to it gets a human review.
Major version bumps always need manual review

Upper bounds on pnpm-workspace.yaml overrides are deliberate: any major update to an override waits under Pending Approval on the Dependency Dashboard instead of opening a branch. Two cases are not held. A 0.x bound (<0.M) is not, because Renovate classes a 0.M to 0.M+1 bump as minor. Vulnerability updates are not either, because Renovate forces dependencyDashboardApproval off for them. So a repository with bounded overrides also needs a CI check that the bounds still hold.
